text:
Cale Makar did not score, and Colorado still won by three. He set up four of the Avalanche's five goals, and when he was on the ice, COL's chances were worth 2.47 expected goals (a measure of shot quality) against 0.62 for CGY. Makar went fourth overall in 2017 out of the Brooks Bandits, and this was the kind of night that pick was meant to produce: 24:24 of work, four assists, and the Avalanche's second win over Calgary this season, after a 7-3 result on Oct. 8.

The game turned in the second period. Colorado had a modest edge after one, with Nathan MacKinnon opening the scoring on a 2% chance, a wrist shot that most nights stays out. Then the Avalanche out-chanced the Flames 1.95 to 0.82 in expected goals over 20 minutes and scored four times in that stretch, including a power-play goal from Martin Necas and a tip-in from Brock Nelson. Artturi Lehkonen added two goals, his second a tip-in at 4:09 of the third that made it 5-2.

Calgary kept trying. Joel Farabee and Martin Pospisil scored to cut it to 4-2, and the Flames finished with 51 shot attempts to Colorado's 58 and a slightly better expected-goals number in the third than the scoreboard suggested. But goalie Arsenii Sergeev faced 4.18 expected goals and allowed five, and the Flames won only 19 of 51 faceoffs. Our numbers give Colorado a 79% chance of winning if this game were replayed, so the result was earned. The facts we have don't include standings or streaks, so we'll leave it at this: Colorado took the season series lead on the strength of one dominant period, and Calgary lost a game it never quite got back into.
